This is the OBD readiness the ECU reports, not a guarantee of passing a legal inspection.

The ECU gives no counters to check this

After a clear the counters start from zero and the monitors need a full drive cycle again. When buying a used car this can hide a fault: ask why the codes were cleared and check again after 100–200 km.
Only one sign: low counters or monitors that are not complete. A disconnected battery gives the same picture; check again after a few trips.
The counters show a long time since the last clear and the monitors are complete.

ECU monitor tests with limits (CAN cars)
The ECU\'s own test results for each monitor: the measured value and its limits. A failed test often comes before a code.
On K-Line cars these results use an older maker-specific format and are not shown. This is normal for such a car.
